english.title: Intentionally alter / suppress / destroy document required to be produced by notice under section 174
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally altered, suppressed, destroyed a document, namely **(..SPECIFY DOCUMENT..), which you had been required to produce by a notice issued under section 174 of the Enterprise Act 2002 on the **(..SPECIFY DATE OF NOTICE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 174A(4) and (6) of the Enterprise Act 2002.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence has been replaced as of 1st January 2025 with the offence under section 116A of the Enterprise Act 2002 (H101975).
(ii) As per subsection 174A(5), a person does not commit an offence under subsection (4) in relation to any act which constitutes a failure to comply with a notice under section 174 if the CMA has proceeded against the person under subsection (1) in relation to that failure.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
